- If sentiment is negative or trending down, model should not forecast upward trend; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- If model shows steady upward drift (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day) with sentiment flat or neutral, check for overconfidence — cap growth rate to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., < -0.2 for 3+ days), model should not ignore mean reversion — shift forecast toward historical mean or 30-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >10% error), model should re-estimate using sentiment-weighted volatility factor — increase downward bias if sentiment is bearish.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show volatility spike, model should reduce forecast slope to avoid “over-optimistic” continuation.
